title: The interplay of selection and dormancy in a Moran model can lead to coexistence of types
summary: In this paper we propose a Moran model that describes the population dynamics of two types: While the first type has a selective advantage during reproduction, the second type can avoid replacement during reproduction with some positive probability by switching temporarily into a dormant state. We investigate the interplay of both evolutionary strategies by studying the invasion dynamics of the dormant type into the resident (selectively advantageous) population in the large population limit of the system.
